newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria says to audit Neftochim oil refinery.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria says to audit Neftochim oil refinery.

text.p: Bulgaria's government on Monday ordered an audit of the country's biggest oil refinery, Neftochim, which posted a loss of 33.4 billion levs ($19.7 million) last year, a senior official said.

Dimitar Bachvarov, deputy president of Neftochim's board of directors, told reporters after the cabinet meeting that last year Neftochim owed 119 billion levs to suppliers and another 37 billion levs in unpaid taxes to the state.
The refinery registered losses of 828.7 million in 1995, officials said.
Bachvarov said Neftochim's losses in 1996 were due mainly to bad pricing policy during the second half of the year as economic crisis deepened.

The new cabinet, which took office in May, ordered the finance ministry to investigate a barter deal exchanging petrol products for wheat, the financing of the refinery's football club Neftochimik, and outstanding payments to the national fund for environmental protection and the road network fund, Bachvarov said.
"The barter deal of petrol products for wheat has had an extremely negative effect on the refinery's finances as the refinery has not received 112 billion levs from the state reserve," he said.

Last year the Neftochimik football club, whose team qualified second in the first division soccer championship this season, received 364 million levs from the refinery, which does not have the right to give subsidies.
Neftochim owes four billion levs to the national environmental fund for 1996 and another 12 billion levs for this year.
The refinery also owes 15 billion levs to the national road network fund.
Deputy Prime Minister and Industry Minister Alexander Bozhkov told reporters the figures in the balance sheet of the refinery did not correspond to the figures of the finance ministry.
Bulgaria suffered a severe petrol shortage in February and March as the refinery, which supplies almost the whole domestic market, lacked cash to buy crude.
Bulgaria plans to offer up to 75 percent of the indebted refinery for sale to private investors. Several firms including Russia's Rosneft have shown interest in the sale.
